correctness.rationale: In each chain factor, powers of the maximal ideal are nested, so two product ideals meet nontrivially exactly when their active supports intersect. A two-set can be total dominating only if the selected ideals are adjacent and their active supports cover every coordinate, because the socle-like singleton-support ideal in any omitted coordinate meets neither. These conditions are sufficient for every nonzero ideal to meet at least one selected ideal. Whenever such a pair exists it is also paired, so both minima are two; direct support choices give exactly the three stated obstructions. For the count, P=prod ell_i(ell_i+2) counts ordered ideal pairs with full support union before vertex exclusions, L=prod ell_i and B=prod(ell_i+1) account for zero/ring cases, L(2^r-2) removes disjoint active-support bipartitions, and L-1 removes proper full-support diagonals. The remainder is even and division by swap gives the displayed formula. Independent arithmetic checks reproduce representative values, including 3 for lengths (1,1,1), 18 for (1,1,1,1), 15 for (2,2) and 40 for (3,1,1). The verifier additionally checks exponent-vector graphs and Z/n through 120; the proof is arbitrary-rank.

final_claim: For a finite commutative principal ideal ring decomposed into chain-ring factors of nilpotency lengths ell_i, a two-ideal set is total dominating exactly when its active supports intersect and cover all factors; outside the field, local-length-two and two-field obstructions this gives gamma_t=gamma_pr=2, all minimum total and paired sets coincide, and their exact number is one half of [prod ell_i(ell_i+2) - (2^r+1)prod ell_i - 2prod(ell_i+1) + 4].
scientific_limitations: A specialized total- or paired-domination paper using different algebraic-graph terminology could contain an equivalent minimum-pair count.
The ring is assumed finite, commutative and principal; arbitrary local ideal lattices need not reduce to active supports.
Only minimum total/paired dominating sets are counted, not all larger such sets.
